record.original_question: For a thermoelastic single crystal undergoing a diffusionless phase transformation at critical temperature θc, determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^qc of the set K(θ) of energy-minimizing deformation gradients for temperatures θ≤θc, including the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θc.

evidence.quote: K(θ) = {A ∈ M+ 3×3 : ψ(A, θ) = 0} be the set of energy-minimizing deformation gradients.
where for a compact set K ⊂ M 3×3 , K qc denotes the quasiconvexification of K.
Problem 16. Determine K(θ)qc for θ ≤ θc .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider a thermoelastic single crystal in three dimensions undergoing a diffusionless (displacive) phase transformation at a critical temperature θ_c. Let M^{3×3} denote the set of real 3×3 matrices and M^{3×3}_+ the subset of matrices with strictly positive determinant. Suppose ψ : M^{3×3}_+ × ℝ → [0,∞) is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density (so ψ(RA,θ) = ψ(A,θ) for every R ∈ SO(3)) which is materially symmetric under the cubic point group, and which for each temperature θ attains its minimum value 0. Define the set of energy-minimizing deformation gradients at temperature θ by

   K(θ) := { A ∈ M^{3×3}_+ : ψ(A,θ) = 0 }.

For a compact set K ⊂ M^{3×3}, its quasiconvexification K^{qc} is defined as

   K^{qc} := { A ∈ M^{3×3} : f(A) ≤ sup_{B ∈ K} f(B) for every quasiconvex f : M^{3×3} → ℝ },

where f : M^{3×3} → ℝ is quasiconvex if for every bounded open Ω ⊂ ℝ^3, every A ∈ M^{3×3}, and every φ ∈ W^{1,∞}_0(Ω;ℝ^3),

   ∫_Ω f(A + ∇φ(x)) dx ≥ |Ω| f(A).

For the cubic-to-tetragonal case at and below θ_c, one has explicitly
   K(θ) = SO(3) U_1(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ)    for θ < θ_c,
   K(θ_c) = SO(3) ∪ SO(3) U_1(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_2(θ_c) ∪ SO(3) U_3(θ_c),
where U_i(θ) = diag(η_2, η_2, η_2) with the entry η_1 in the i-th diagonal position (η_1, η_2 > 0 temperature-dependent stretch parameters with η_1 ≠ η_2 for θ < θ_c, and η_1 = η_2 = 1 at θ = θ_c giving the austenite identity).

Problem. Determine the quasiconvexification K(θ)^{qc} explicitly for all θ ≤ θ_c, in particular for the cubic-to-tetragonal three-well case (and the four-well case at θ = θ_c that also includes SO(3)).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as open. While the two-well quasiconvexification (relevant to e.g. orthorhombic-to-monoclinic transitions) has been computed via minors relations, the three-well cubic-to-tetragonal case—and the four-well case including SO(3) at θ = θ_c—remains unresolved. Partial results, such as characterizing rank-one connections between SO(3) and K(θ)^{qc} (Ball–Carstensen) and other structural properties, are known, but a complete explicit description of K(θ)^{qc} is not available.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical models of martensitic microstructure (J. M. Ball)
status_evidence.snippet: In the case when there are just two martensitic variants ... K^{qc} can be calculated. Even though K^{qc} is unknown in the case of three tetragonal wells ...
status_evidence.claim: The three-well quasiconvexification for the cubic-to-tetragonal case is unknown.

status_evidence.title: Nonclassical Austenite-Martensite Interfaces (Ball & Carstensen)
status_evidence.snippet: reduces to determining the possible rank-one connections between SO(3) and the quasiconvexification K(θ)^{qc}.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial structural information on K(θ)^{qc} (e.g. rank-one connections to SO(3)) has been established.
